subject: Finly discovery recap - p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Finly discovery recap - p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Hi Alex - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we have alignment.

Key pain points you shared:
- Real-time streaming UX for your customers is suffering: first-byte and token streaming feels sluggish on complex prompts.
- Current p95 generation latency is ~800-1,200ms on your fleet for standard prompts; streaming cold-starts can be worse.
- Concurrency: you expect to hit ~350-500 concurrent live sessions in peak campaigns (web + mobile).
- Cost and predictability: you're trying to avoid a 2x cost spike if you provision for peak.

Current stack notes (as discussed):
- Self-hosted LLMs on GCP (custom inference infra) using mixed instance types.
- Model variant: open LLM fine-tuned in-house; KV cache mostly disabled due to prompt variability.
- You're shipping partial streaming via application-level chunking which increases tail latency.

Success criteria you called out:
- p95 first-byte (stream start) < 200ms for 90% of production traffic; overall p95 token latency < 300ms for core flows.
- Support 400 concurrent streaming sessions with 95th percentile SLOs met without massive overprovision.
- Streaming UX: sub-200ms first-chunk for interactive experiences.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical deep dive with your infra/ML eng team - Aditya to lead - to review traces and request/response shapes.
2) Share current traces + config (we discussed a sanitized bundle) - attached: finly-current-infra-traces.zip.
3) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones: PoC, perf tuning, baseline, rollout - attached: 20260214-finly-map-draft.pdf.
4) Proposed timeline: 2-week PoC, followed by a focused optimization sprint.

Resources we'll bring:
- Aditya (solutions engineer) will propose batching, KV/prefix caching options, quantization profiles, and suggested routing policies.
- A short deep-dive agenda attached.

Please confirm any missing items and share 2-3 windows next week for a 60-90 minute technical deep dive with your infra team.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: 20260214-finly-map-draft.pdf (application/pdf) - draft MAP
Attachments: finly-current-infra-traces.zip (application/zip) - sanitized traces and perf logs

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finly.com>, infra-team@finly.com
Date: 2026-02-14T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap - p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa - great summary and thanks for pulling the MAP together. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Our hard success criteria are: first-byte p95 (stream start) < 150ms for desktop web flows and < 250ms for mobile. Overall token p95 target of ~250-300ms for the most-common prompts.
- Concurrency: target steady-state 350 concurrent streaming sessions; plan for 500 as a stress target.
- Important: streaming UX also needs deterministic ordering and near-real-time partial results (we currently send deltas but hit reordering on retries).

We will upload sanitized traces to the S3 link you provided and can also share our request/response sizes. Priya and infra-team will be on the deep dive. Available windows next week: Tue 2026-02-17 10:00-12:00 PT, Wed 2026-02-18 09:00-11:00 PT.

One ask: can your team include any benchmark examples for streaming first-byte vs total-token p95 on similar workloads? Even ballpark numbers will help set expectations before the PoC.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, Finly
alex.johnson@finly.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Finly discovery recap - p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Thanks Alex - appreciate the clarity on targets. A few preliminary notes ahead of the deep dive:
- We'll want the traces (thanks) plus a few sample prompt sizes and median/95th token counts so we can estimate KV cache hit potential.
- Likely levers to meet your targets: continuous batching tuned for short-latency paths, prefix/KV caching where sensible, early-first-token optimization (kernel selection + small-batch fast-path), and selective model quantization.
- For concurrency: we may recommend a mixed fleet + smart routing that favors lower-latency instances for interactive streaming and cheaper instances for low-priority batch workloads to control costs.

Attached is a short deep-dive agenda and the items we'll want to review.

Proposed deep-dive slots we can cover on Tue 02/17 10:00-11:30 PT (match your slot) - if that works let's lock and I'll send a calendar invite and a shared Confluence page for notes.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

--

Thanks Aditya - Tue 02/17 10:00-11:30 PT works for the deep dive. We'll upload sanitized traces and a small sample dataset by EOD tomorrow.

Two additional asks before the session:
1) Can you include an example PoC scope that outlines what success looks like (test harness, sample workloads, pass/fail criteria)?
2) Can you provide any existing streaming benchmark numbers you have for comparable interactive workloads (ballpark is fine)?

We prefer to have our infra lead (cc'ed) on the session and Priya will handle scheduling. Looking forward to the deep dive.

- Alex
